oneLiner: The enterprise and defense operating system for AI agents, growing near 100% at 60%+ adjusted margins. The market is betting that US commercial demand compounds for years, so that FY2027-28 earnings grow into a multiple no other large-cap software company carries.

verdict.summary: Nothing in Q3 2026 weakens the business case: growth accelerated again and US commercial overtook US government. The problem is the price, not the company. Our base case (FY2027 revenue +50%, a mid-70s multiple on GAAP EPS at end-2027) lands near today's level, and the probability-weighted value sits slightly below it, because the bear case loses more than half while the bull case adds about 40%. Two things would move us to Positive: US commercial growth holding above 120% into Q4 with bookings re-accelerating, or a reset in price that puts the base case 25%+ above it. We would turn Cautious if US commercial falls below ~90% growth or the near-zero tax rate starts to show up in EPS without margin offset.
wtb: FY2027 revenue of at least ~$12.5B (+47% on the ~$8.53B FY2026 guide), which needs US commercial to keep growing near 100% for most of the year.
GAAP net margin stays at or above ~45% in FY2027 even as the effective tax rate rises from ~1% (Q3 2026) toward a normal rate.
Shorter contracts expand as Karp claims: US commercial remaining deal value keeps growing faster than 50% YoY through Q2 2027.
The market still pays 70x+ trailing GAAP EPS at end-2027, which requires FY2028 growth to look like 35%+ at that point.

bear.why: Growth halves to ~35% as AIP pilots saturate, shorter contracts fail to expand and a federal budget impasse slows government awards. Net margin falls to ~40% as tax expense normalizes. A 35% grower still earns a premium, but the market stops paying for the 2028-30 outer years.

base.why: Revenue +50%: US commercial decelerates from ~148% toward ~80% on a larger base, government grows ~35% on Army EA, Maven and TITAN. Net margin ~46% as operating leverage offsets a rising tax rate. With 40%+ growth still visible for FY2028, the market keeps paying a mid-70s multiple.

bull.why: Revenue +64%: AIP becomes the default enterprise agent platform, US commercial stays above 100% and Golden Dome and NGC2 convert into large production programs. Net margin holds ~50% and FY2028 looks like another 50% year, so the multiple stays near the 2025-26 range.

scenarioModel.note: FY2026 revenue = Q1 $1.63B + Q2 $1.94B + Q3 $2.31B + Q4 guide $2.65B = ~$8.53B. EPS = FY2027 revenue x GAAP net margin / ~2.60B diluted shares (2.57B in Q3 2026 plus ~1% dilution): bear 11.5 x 40% / 2.60 = 1.77; base 12.8 x 46% / 2.60 = 2.26; bull 14.0 x 50% / 2.60 = 2.69. Multiples are applied to FY2027 GAAP EPS at end-2027. Scenario inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: How long can US commercial grow faster than 100%?
debates.bull: US commercial accelerated sequentially for another quarter (+29% q/q in Q3 2026) and overtook US government; customers buy without a large sales force, and remaining deal value is $6.5B.
debates.bear: The base is now ~$1B a quarter; the comparison in 2027 is against +148% growth, and AI agent budgets at large enterprises are being contested by Databricks, Snowflake, Microsoft and the model labs themselves.
debates.view: This is the debate that sets the multiple. The base case needs ~80% US commercial growth in FY2027; anything below ~90% exiting 2026 puts the bear case in play.

signpost.metric: Q4 2026 US commercial revenue growth YoY

debates.q: Do shorter contracts and a TCV dip foreshadow slower growth?
debates.bull: Shorter first contracts close faster and expand: Karp's 'once you go Palantir, you don't go back'. Revenue, not TCV, is what compounds, and US commercial RDV still grew 79% YoY.
debates.bear: Total TCV grew only 6% YoY in Q3 2026 and US commercial TCV fell to $1.46B from a record $2.13B in Q2 while revenue nearly doubled; bookings lagging revenue is usually the first sign of deceleration.
debates.view: One quarter of lumpy TCV is not a trend, but RDV growth has slowed to +4% q/q. If RDV stalls for another quarter, our FY2027 base revenue is too high.

signpost.metric: US commercial remaining deal value growth (YoY and q/q)
signpost.threshold: below +50% YoY or a second quarter under +5% q/q = cut base revenue

debates.q: How much of GAAP EPS is durable?
debates.bull: Adjusted operating margin is 62% and adjusted FCF (~53% of Q3 revenue) exceeds net income; cash conversion is healthy at ~113% TTM, so the profit is real.
debates.bear: Net income runs above operating income (115% TTM; Q3 2026 net income $1.13B vs operating income $1.09B) because of ~$89M of quarterly interest income, investment marks and a tax provision of only $13.6M (~1%). SBC of $319M a quarter is excluded from adjusted figures.
debates.view: A real but slow-moving issue: a normal tax rate takes roughly a fifth off EPS, which is why our base uses a 46% net margin, below Q3's 49%. It moves the value if the tax rate jumps faster than operating leverage grows.

signpost.metric: Effective tax rate and net income / operating income
signpost.threshold: tax rate above 15% in FY2027 guidance with no margin offset = lower base EPS

thesis: AIP is winning enterprise agent deployment. US commercial reached $984M in Q3 2026 and passed US government for the first time; it has more than quintupled in two years.
Growth is still accelerating at scale. Total revenue growth went from +85% to +93% to +96% over the last three quarters, and the FY2026 guide was raised from $8.15B to ~$8.53B.
Government is moving from prototype to production. The $10B/10-year Army Enterprise Agreement, NATO Maven, NGC2 and the Sep 2026 TITAN production orders embed Palantir in programs of record.
Operating leverage is elite. Adjusted operating margin held at 62% and GAAP operating margin at 47% while revenue nearly doubled, with capex under 1% of revenue.

points: Revenue $2.31B, +96% YoY, +20% QoQ, vs $2.18B consensus (LSEG) and a $2.16B guide.

latestProse: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 30; reported Nov 2). Revenue $2.31B, +96% YoY and +20% QoQ, the first quarter above $2B, beating $2.18B consensus and the $2.16B guide. US commercial $984M (+148%, +29% QoQ) overtook US government $953M (+96%). GAAP operating margin 47%, adjusted 62%, Rule of 40 158. GAAP net income $1.13B ($0.44 per diluted share on 2.57B shares). Bookings were the soft spot: total TCV $2.92B (+6% YoY) and US commercial TCV fell to $1.46B from a record $2.13B in Q2, which Karp attributed to shorter initial contracts that expand later. Net dollar retention of 165% and 686 US commercial customers were reported by secondary sources but are not in the release (unverified). Shares fell in the session after the print despite the beat.
guidanceProse: FY2026 guide raised to $8.530-8.534B (~+91%) from $8.15B, against ~$8.20B consensus before the print; US commercial above $3.559B (at least +143%); adjusted operating income $5.245-5.249B; adjusted FCF $4.8-5.0B. Q4 2026 guide: revenue $2.649-2.653B (+88% YoY) and adjusted operating income $1.640-1.644B, implying a ~62% adjusted margin. Management again guided GAAP operating income and net income positive every quarter but gave no FY2027 framework. Pre-print analyst estimates had FY2027 revenue around $12.3B (+50%) (unverified).
segments: US government ~41% of Q3 2026 revenue ($953M): Army Enterprise Agreement, Maven, TITAN, NGC2; plus allied defense (NATO Maven, UK).
US commercial ($984M in Q3 2026) is the growth engine on AIP adoption; the expanded PwC alliance adds enterprise distribution.
International commercial is the laggard: $182M in Q2 2026, +26% YoY (Q3 figure not in the release).
competitive: Enterprise AI platforms: Databricks, Snowflake Cortex and Microsoft Fabric target the same data and AI budgets; model labs selling agents directly are a newer threat.
Defense tech: Anduril is partner and rival - the two split the Sep 2026 TITAN production orders ($127M to Palantir, $65M to Anduril) after jointly winning Army NGC2 work.
The big consultancies compete for AI-implementation budgets; Palantir's forward-deployed model positions it as software rather than billable hours, and the PwC alliance co-opts one of them.
C3.ai has faded as a serious threat.
moat: The ontology layer binding an institution's data, logic and actions creates switching costs once operational workflows run through Foundry and AIP. In government: decades of accreditations, classified deployments and contract vehicles newcomers cannot replicate quickly - and with TITAN, a hardware delivery program that embeds Palantir in the Army's deep-sensing architecture rather than alongside it.
risks: Multiple compression. EV/sales sits far above its own 10-year median (peer chart); a deceleration from ~96% to ~50% growth can halve the multiple even as earnings rise (the bear case).
Bookings lag revenue. Total TCV grew only 6% YoY in Q3 2026 while revenue grew 96%; if shorter contracts do not expand, FY2027 growth undershoots the base case.

EPS flattered by below-the-line items. TTM net income is 115% of operating income on interest income, investment marks and a ~1% tax rate; normalization costs roughly a fifth of EPS, and SBC ($319M in Q3 2026) is excluded from adjusted metrics. Michael Burry has publicly criticized the accounting (reported).
Government and budget dependency. US government is ~41% of revenue; a continuing resolution or budget fight in federal FY2027 slows new awards in the second-largest segment.
Persistent insider selling. Insiders sold roughly $117M of stock in the 90 days to early Sep 2026 (unverified), continuing a pattern of zero open-market buys.
catalysts: Dec 2026: federal FY2027 appropriations or continuing resolution - pace of new defense awards (risk 4).
Early Feb 2027: Q4 2026 report - US commercial growth vs the 90-120% band (debate 1), RDV and TCV (debate 2), FY2027 guide.
Feb 2027: FY2026 10-K - effective tax rate and investment gains (debate 3).
Through 2027: TITAN deliveries (eight systems over 18 months), Golden Dome awards, NGC2 next-phase decision around mid-2027.

valPresets.note: Even the bear preset needs 25% year-one FCF growth; the reverse DCF says ~32% constant FCF growth for a decade is priced in, close to the 3-year revenue track record. That asymmetry is the entire PLTR debate.
